hero.title: CDN Content Delivery Network
hero.subtitle: Global edge acceleration for a faster, more resilient web presence
hero.desc: Kineticlinks CDN combines over 100 edge nodes worldwide with intelligent routing to cache static and dynamic content closer to your users, cutting latency and boosting load times. Built-in terabit-scale DDoS protection keeps your service stable through traffic spikes and malicious attacks alike.

overview.title: What Is a CDN?
overview.p1: A CDN (Content Delivery Network) is a network of edge servers distributed across multiple regions. When a user visits your site, the CDN routes the request to the node physically closest to them instead of forcing every request back to a single origin server, shortening the data path, reducing latency, and easing the load on your origin infrastructure.
overview.p2: Kineticlinks operates over 100 edge nodes across Asia-Pacific, North America, and Europe, using intelligent routing to continuously measure latency and congestion at each node and automatically select the fastest path. Whether your users are in Taiwan, mainland China, Southeast Asia, or Western markets, they get access speeds close to a local server.
overview.p3: Beyond acceleration, a CDN is also your first line of defense against distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attacks. Kineticlinks provides terabit-scale scrubbing capacity that filters malicious traffic at the edge before it ever reaches your origin server, keeping your business running without interruption.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.q1: Is a CDN worth it for a small website?
faq.a1: Yes. CDN benefits aren't limited to large sites — even a small or mid-sized site with visitors overseas or in other regions will see a noticeable improvement in load time and user experience.
faq.q2: Is CDN setup complicated? Do I need to change hosts or code?
faq.a2: No hosting change is required. In most cases you only need to update your domain's DNS to route traffic to the CDN — your origin server and codebase stay untouched, and setup is usually completed within a business day.

overview.title: What Is a VPS?
overview.p1: A VPS (Virtual Private Server) uses virtualization to divide a single physical server into multiple independent virtual environments. Unlike shared hosting, a VPS gives each user a dedicated allocation of CPU cores, memory, and storage, delivering near-bare-metal performance with full system control — at a fraction of the cost of standing up your own physical server.
overview.p2: Kineticlinks VPS instances run entirely on NVMe SSD storage, far outperforming traditional SATA SSD and HDD in read/write speed, paired with modern high-clock-speed CPUs to cut response times for database queries, page rendering, and application workloads. Every plan supports online scaling of CPU, memory, and disk space to match traffic growth without downtime.
overview.p3: To minimize data loss risk, every VPS instance includes scheduled automatic backups and snapshots, preserving multiple recovery points so you can restore quickly after an incident — letting your team focus on building the product instead of routine infrastructure upkeep.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.q1: What's the difference between a VPS and shared hosting?
faq.a1: Shared hosting means multiple users draw from the same pool of hardware resources, so you can be affected by other sites' traffic. A VPS uses virtualization to give each user a dedicated allocation of CPU, memory, and storage — more stable performance and full system-level control.
faq.q2: Can I upgrade my VPS specs later?
faq.a2: Yes. As your business grows and needs more compute, you can adjust CPU, memory, and disk capacity online, and in most cases the upgrade completes without downtime or redeployment.
faq.q3: How is data safety handled on a VPS?
faq.a3: Every VPS instance includes scheduled automatic backups and snapshots, preserving multiple historical recovery points so you can restore quickly if something goes wrong, minimizing operational disruption.

overview.title: What Is IDC Data Center Buildout?
overview.p1: IDC (Internet Data Center) buildout means planning and constructing a dedicated facility environment — with complete power, cooling, fire suppression, networking, and physical security infrastructure — for a company's own or outsourced server equipment. Compared to simply renting standard cabinet space in an existing facility or public cloud, a custom IDC buildout can be planned around a company's specific regulatory, data sovereignty, and performance requirements.
overview.p2: Kineticlinks buildout projects start with upfront network architecture planning and BGP dual-line bandwidth design, helping clients evaluate the best facility location and power specification, then coordinating hardware procurement and rack cabling to ensure the overall architecture is highly available and ready for future expansion.
overview.p3: Once the facility is live, we continue providing 24/7 on-site monitoring and operational support, tracking power, temperature, humidity, and network status in real time, with standardized incident response procedures so your core systems run in a stable, well-controlled physical environment.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.q1: I have zero cloud experience — can you plan this from scratch?
faq.a1: Yes. We start by understanding your current architecture and business needs, then provide full consulting and hands-on support from initial cloud service selection through architecture design and ongoing operations.
faq.q2: Will a cloud migration cause service downtime?
faq.a2: We plan a phased migration strategy based on system dependencies and test and validate everything before the official cutover, minimizing downtime — critical systems can also run in parallel during the transition to ensure a smooth handoff.
faq.q3: When does hybrid cloud make more sense than going fully public cloud?
faq.a3: If your organization has regulatory requirements to keep data on-premises, hasn't finished depreciating existing hardware investments, or has systems that are extremely latency-sensitive, a hybrid architecture lets public cloud and your own facility complement each other.
faq.q4: Can you help optimize an existing cloud bill?
faq.a4: Yes. We audit current resource usage to identify idle resources, oversized instances, or opportunities like reserved instances that reduce cost, and provide concrete optimization recommendations.
faq.q5: Is cloud architecture consulting a one-time project or an ongoing engagement?
